name: brokerage_orders_list
title: Find orders on an account
description: Returns orders on one account, filtered by lifecycle state, symbol, or date, most recent first. Use when the customer asks whether a trade went through, what orders are still working, what they traded recently, or why something was rejected — and use it first whenever you need an orderId for another tool. Do not use for holdings — call brokerage_positions_list, because an order becomes a position only once it fills and a filled order is not the same as a current holding. Do not use for cash movements — call brokerage_transactions_list. status WORKING covers every non-terminal state and is what the customer means by open orders. Terminal states are FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, and REPLACED; an order in a terminal state will never change again and must not be polled. New status values may be added over time: treat any status you do not recognise as still working, never as terminal. filledQuantity and remainingQuantity together describe a partial fill, which is a common and non-obvious state — an order can be both working and partly filled. Rejected orders carry a rejectReason with a machine-readable code. An empty array means no orders matched the filter, which is a successful answer. Reads only.

accountId.description: The account whose orders to read. Obtain it from brokerage_accounts_list.

status.description: Filter to one lifecycle state. WORKING covers every non-terminal state including partially filled. Omitted returns every order in the date window.

symbol.description: Filter to one underlying ticker, uppercase. Matches the underlying for option orders. Omitted returns every symbol.

fromDate.description: Earliest order creation date, inclusive, in US Eastern time. Omitted means seven days ago. The window may not exceed 90 days.

toDate.description: Latest order creation date, inclusive, in US Eastern time. Omitted means today.

pageSize.description: Maximum orders to return, most recent first. Omitted returns up to 25.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous result's completeness.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

decimal.description: A decimal number as a string, to avoid binary floating-point error.

accountId.description: The account these orders belong to.

asOf.description: The instant this view of the order book was true (UTC).

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency for every monetary value in this result.

orders.description: Matching orders, most recently created first.

orderId.description: Order identifier. Pass to brokerage_order_get for full detail including executions.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Known values: PENDING_NEW, NEW, PARTIALLY_FILLED, PENDING_CANCEL, PENDING_REPLACE, SUSPENDED, FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, REPLACED. Treat an unrecognised value as still working.

isTerminal.description: True when the order can never change again. Use this rather than comparing the status string, and never poll a terminal order.

side.description: Direction. Option orders use the explicit open and close forms because they drive margin treatment.

symbol.description: Ticker, or the option's underlying ticker.

description.description: Human-readable description of what was ordered, such as AAPL 18 Dec 2026 250 Call.

quantity.description: Ordered quantity: shares for equities, contracts for options. Always positive; direction is in side.

filledQuantity.description: How much has executed so far. Greater than zero with a non-terminal status means a partial fill.

remainingQuantity.description: How much is still working. Zero on a terminal order.

limitPrice.description: Limit price, when the order type has one.

stopPrice.description: Stop trigger price, when the order type has one.

averageFillPrice.description: Volume-weighted average price of the executions so far. This is the price the customer actually got.

timeInForce.description: How long the order stays live. DAY expires at the close; GTC persists across sessions.

rejectReason.description: Present only when status is REJECTED.

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason, such as INSUFFICIENT_BUYING_POWER or MARKET_CLOSED.

truncated.description: True when more orders matched than were returned.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page. Null on the last page.

narrowingHint.description: How to narrow the query to a complete answer, when truncated.

completeness.description: How much of the matching set this result contains.
